{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

#FLUX --nodes=1
#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=8
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=12
# NOTE: SLURM's '--mem=0' requests all available memory on the node. This is
# the equivalent behavior in Flux.
#FLUX --mem-per-node=0
#FLUX --gpus=8

# NOTE: Flux does not have a token for nodename in the output/error file paths.
# The SLURM %N token has been omitted. Also, the output and error streams were
# swapped in the original script; this has been corrected.
#FLUX -o {name}-{id}.out
#FLUX -e {name}-{id}.err

source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh

# Use partition/queue name to load OS-specific modulespath to use to override
# login node environment. The SLURM variable $SLURM_JOB_PARTITION has been
# replaced with the Flux equivalent, $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE.
if [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i ubuntu) = *Ubuntu* ]]; then
    module use /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i rhel8) = *RHEL8* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i rhel9) = *RHEL9* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i sles15) = *SLES15* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i centos8) = *CentOS8* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
elif [[ $(echo $FLUX_JOB_QUEUE | grep -i rocky9) = *Rocky9* ]]; then
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/ubuntu/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel8/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/rhel9/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/sles15sp4/modulefiles
    module unuse /shared/apps/modules/centos8/modulefiles
    module use /shared/apps/modules/rocky9/modulefiles
fi


module purge
module load rocm/5.4.2

tmp=/tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$
mkdir -p $tmp

# Example with MPI: STMV Benchmark
mkdir -p /tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$/stmv
singularity run /shared/apps/bin/gromacs_2022.3.amd1_161.sif tar -xvf /benchmarks/stmv/stmv.tar.gz -C /tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$/stmv 1>/dev/null

# The singularity command is now launched with 'flux run' instead of the container's mpirun.
# Flux will manage the MPI launch across the 8 allocated tasks.
singularity run /shared/apps/bin/gromacs_2022.3.amd1_161.sif flux run gmx_mpi mdrun -pin on -nsteps 100000 -resetstep 90000 -ntomp 8 -noconfout -nb gpu -bonded cpu -pme gpu -npme 1 -v -nstlist 400 -gpu_id 01234567 -s /tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$/stmv/topol.tpr -g /tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$/stmv/md.log -e /tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$/stmv/ener.eder -cpo /tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$/stmv/state.cpt

# The SLURM variables have been replaced with the Flux equivalents.
cp -r /tmp/$USER/gpu8-$$   $PWD/gpu8-$$-$FLUX_JOB_NODELIST-$FLUX_JOB_ID

# Do the clean-up
/bin/rm -rf $tmp
"
}

Flux allocates a specific GPU to each of the 8 tasks and uses environment variables (e.g., `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES`) to ensure each task has exclusive access to its assigned device. By hardcoding the IDs, the script will likely cause all 8 tasks to conflict over the same physical devices instead of using their dedicated resources, leading to severe performance degradation or failure. The `-gpu_id` flag should be removed.

There is a resource mismatch between allocated CPUs and utilized threads. The job requests 12 CPUs per task (`--cpus-per-task=12`), but the application is configured to use only 8 OpenMP threads (`-ntomp 8`). This leaves 4 CPUs per task (32 CPUs total) allocated but idle, wasting a significant amount of compute resources. The request should be reduced to `--cpus-per-task=8` to match the application's needs.
